Home.heroTitle: Postcards you won't find in a shop.
Home.heroText: I draw them myself. Some in runs of twenty, some just once. I ship everywhere Postcrossing reaches.
Home.feature2Text: Once it's sold out, I don't reprint it.
Home.feature3Text: Rigid envelope, 2–3 days to the post office.
Home.emptyShop: The shop is filling up soon.
Home.postcrossingText: Packages of 10 and 20 postcards, all different. Standard back layout, without my logo taking over half the card.
Home.review1Quote: Arrived in Finland in nine days, packaged perfectly. The back is finally blank the way it should be.
Home.review2Quote: Bought the package of 20 and couldn't bear to let any of them go. Ordered another one.
Home.review3Quote: The cardstock is thick, the colors match the site exactly. That rarely happens.

About.paragraph1: I started with a single postcard for a Postcrossing swap. When someone asked if I could make ten more, I printed my first batch.
About.paragraph2: I draw everything myself, digitally and in watercolor. I print in Zemun, in batches of up to thirty. A few designs stay one-of-a-kind — I don't reprint those.
About.stepsHeading: How a postcard comes to be
About.step1Text: In pencil, usually on the train. Most stay in the notebook.
About.step2Text: Two to three weeks per design. I pick the colors last.
About.step3Text: Matte 300 g cardstock, a test print then the batch. I number them by hand.
About.wholesaleText: Wholesale from 50 pieces up, price list on request.
